subject: chemistry
question_text: A solution is prepared by adding 2 g of a substance A to 18 g of H₂O. Calculate the mass percentage of the solute.

verification.note: Chapter 5 (Stoichiometry) is sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack chemistry section (book pp.66-72), which prints the question, its star rank and a model answer. Only ONE source book is held for chemistry — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only — so the two-book union check is PENDING a second chemistry source. This chapter has NO Long Answer section in the book, so no 8-mark form is invented. The 1+1 mark split is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented. AI chemistry check 2026-08-25 (audit round 3): the insider note claimed nothing else in the arithmetic can go wrong, while the card’s own common mistakes list three more (forgetting × 100, writing 0.1 and stopping, writing 10 with no % sign). The overclaim is removed and the insider note now names the answer-mark requirement instead. No marked line changed.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Formula and substitution

lines.text: Mass % of solute = (mass of solute / mass of solution) × 100

lines: Mass of solution = mass of A + mass of water
steps.why: The denominator is the mass of the whole SOLUTION, so the solute's own 2 g must be added to the 18 g of water before dividing.
common_mistakes: Dividing by 18 (the solvent alone) instead of 20 (the solution) and answering 11.1%.
steps.memory_tip: Solution = solute + solvent. The bottom of the fraction is always the total 20, never the water alone.
steps.margin_note: The 2 + 18 = 20 line is where this mark is decided.

steps.label: The answer
steps.why: 2 out of 20 is one tenth, and one tenth expressed as a percentage is 10%.
common_mistakes: Writing 0.1 and stopping. The question asks for a percentage.
steps.memory_tip: 2 in every 20 is the same as 10 in every 100.

insider_note: The examiner reads the denominator first: 20 earns the method mark, 18 loses it. The arithmetic after that is short, but it is not automatic: the answer mark needs the × 100 and the % sign, so 0.1 or a bare 10 does not earn it.
